svg.title: Variational effective-field derivation vs additive direct spin-torque composition on the LLG RHS
svg.desc: Three-panel diagram illustrating how conservative micromagnetic energy functionals E_k[m] produce field-form contributions H_k via delta E_k = -mu0 int M_s H_k . eta dV and sum into H_eff, while non-conservative current-driven torques enter separately via a single Gilbert-to-explicit conversion into tau_direct on the tangent plane T_m S^2 of the LLG right-hand side.
svg.text: Effective-Field Variational Composition vs. Direct Spin-Torque RHS
Strict separation of conservative energy variation (Heff in A/m) and non-conservative direct torques (τdirect in s-1)
Energy functional E[m] → directional derivative → Hk (A/m)
1. Total Energy Functional E[m] = ∑k ∈ K Ek[m] (J)
Exchange · Demag · Zeeman · Uniaxial/Cubic · DMI · Magnetoelastic
Each term owns its SI density wk, sign, and natural surface boundary law
2. First Variation on Admissible Tangent η (m · η = 0)
δEk[m; η] = −μ0 ∫Ωm Ms Hk · η dV
• FDM: finite-difference / convolution stencil evaluated at cell centers
• FEM: weak residual rk projected via lumped mass Hk = −(μ0Ms)-1 Mlump-1 rk
3. Effective-Field Accumulator (plus non-energy fields Hoe, Hth)
Heff(x, t) = ∑k ∈ Kfield Hk(x, t) [A m-1]
CDL = Ω0(ξDL − αξFL)/(1+α2), CFL = Ω0(ξFL + αξDL)/(1+α2)
• Never inject τdirect as an effective field in Heff
Bypassed in pure relaxation / minimization stages
